articles.title: What Cedric Robinson’s Black Marxism Gets Wrong
articles.author: August H. Nimtz
articles.content_excerpt: Cedric Robinson’s Black Marxism: The Making of the Black Radical Tradition did not receive widespread attention after its original publication in 1983. Since 2000, when it was republished with a new preface and an introduction by historian Robin D. G. Kelley, however, the book has enjoyed widespread appeal and influence in the anglophone humanities and social sciences as well as among activists. Robinson’s proposed theory of “racial capitalism” and his framework of a “black radical tradition” have shaped debates about racial inequalities in capitalist societies and Marxism’s potential for anti-racist politics in recent decades. articles.title: History From Below: Molly Crabapple’s Here Where We Live Is Our Country
articles.author: DSA Religion and Socialism Working Group
articles.content_excerpt: There is little new to say about Molly Crabapple’s wonderful history of the Jewish Bund , Here Where We Live is Our Country . Since its publication, the book has been widely celebrated by the Left, dismissed by the Right, and met with a mix of praise and accusations of naivety or idealism from liberal and centrist publications. The praise is well deserved. Crabapple writes so joyfully and tenderly about the Bund that a passive reading of the book feels almost heretical. The Bund was anti-Zionist, and Here Where We Live is Our Country is the kind of book that inspires people to continue the struggle against Zionism and genocide. articles.title: Amazon Workers Keep Walking Out
articles.content_excerpt: RIVERSIDE, CALIF. — In February, a worker at Amazon’s DJT 6 delivery station in Riverside was confronted inside the warehouse by a former coworker. She had accused him of harassment. The man had already been fired but somehow got back inside the building. Emmanuel Cadena, who works at DJT 6 and knew the woman, said the man blamed her for his firing. Another worker stepped in. “ He flashed the gun and said, ​ ‘ If you and your friend have a problem, you can see me outside,’” Cadena said. The confrontation happened near the conveyor belt where workers were sorting packages. Amazon did not pause work, according to Cadena. ​ “ There’s no sort of cover in any capacity,” he said. articles.title: The Uprising We Got vs. the One We Need
articles.author: Eileen Jones
articles.content_excerpt: How do you make a boring film about a peasant revolt? Writer-director Paul Greengrass ( The Bourne Supremacy , Captain Phillips , United 93 ) has found a way. His new film, The Uprising , is about the English Peasants’ Revolt of 1381, and it’s such a glum plod I should’ve forgotten it immediately after seeing it. But somehow it haunts me. Maybe it’s the dismal blue-lit cinematography, so typical of our spiritless era. And on top of that, Greengrass’s tendency to favor in intense scenes his wobbling, uncertain handheld-camera work that has so little impact, you want to yell at the screen, “Pick a shot, man! articles.title: How Should Socialists Relate to the Market?
articles.author: Vivek Chibber
articles.content_excerpt: It’s all too common for people to associate the existence of markets with capitalism. But because we know markets had a life before capitalism, we can also imagine them having a life after. On this latest episode of the Jacobin Radio podcast Confronting Capitalism , Vivek Chibber and Melissa Naschek compare how markets operated in precapitalist economies versus modern capitalist economies to see if markets may prove useful in future socialist societies. Confronting Capitalism with Vivek Chibber is produced by Catalyst: A Journal of Theory and Strategy and published by Jacobin . You can listen to the full episode here . articles.author: California DSA
articles.content_excerpt: OCDSA’s Mutual Aid Committee, affectionately abbreviated to “MAC”, has been one of the chapter’s longest operating undertakings. Following the Marxist ideal of a society sharing goods and services according to ability and need, MAC’s work, directly within the chapter and with members of the community at large, has long been the focus of the group, even before our formal establishment as a committee in 2026. MAC works with community partners to provide meals and groceries to the county’s at-risk and unhoused populations. What does MAC do? In the pandemic years, MAC provided taillight services for free to the community in the wake of George Floyd’s murder, and helped provide groceries to low-income community members directly at their doors during lockdown. articles.author: California DSA
articles.content_excerpt: Every so often we have an opportunity to do something transformative. I’m not talking about “changing the narrative”, although that’s important and part of the picture. I’m talking about changing the world. Easy to say, hard to do. East Bay DSA and the Alameda Labor Council joined forces to launch the first Tax the Rich canvass in Oakland September 19, two days after the chapter’s art build created the signage. articles.title: Kingston’s Quiet Rent Revolution
articles.content_excerpt: KINGSTON, N.Y. — On September 1 , John and Gail Bechtold tore open their monthly rent statement, hoping their landlord had finally given in and fixed it. But those same four numbers stared back at them: $ 1 , 700 . It was the 39 th month in a row that Opus Management Group overcharged the Bechtolds by $ 221 . 74 for their apartment in the Dutch Village (or, as Gail calls it, Dump Village) complex in Kingston. According to a state housing agency ruling, Opus owes the Bechtolds, both retirees in their 80 s, well over $ 10 , 000 . articles.title: The Foundations of Turkey’s Peace With the Kurds Are Shaky
articles.author: Ertuğrul Kürkçü
articles.content_excerpt: Turkey’s political scene is moving. The recently passed Framework Law redirects the Kurdish question — the principal fault line in the country’s imagined national unity — from armed confrontation to regulated pacification. This has political consequences far beyond its narrow legal scope. More than bringing one period of the Kurdish conflict to a close, it opens a new phase in Turkey’s class struggles by reshaping the balance between the state, the Kurdish movement, and the political opposition. The August 10 Framework Law — officially the Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion — is a genuine rupture in Turkey’s handling of the Kurdish conflict.
